title: Smoke-wrapper map retains stale documentation line anchors
observed_behavior: The canonical generate_smoke_wrapper_map --check command exits 1 because five stored line numbers no longer match their current documentation inputs, even though all recorded browser wrapper/module/direct-only counts still match disk.
expected_invariant: Tracked generated navigation and drift evidence must agree byte-for-byte with its current authoritative inputs whenever its maintained non-mutating --check gate is run.
root_cause: Active inventory and testing documents gained lines after the last map generation, but docs/generated/SMOKE_WRAPPER_MAP.json was not regenerated in the same change.
failure_scenario: An operator or maintainer follows a generated line anchor and lands on unrelated text, while phase/release generated checks fail late despite the underlying counts remaining correct.
evidence: Bundled-Python generate_smoke_wrapper_map --check exited 1 and emitted an exact unified diff for five line-only changes.
Current artifact SHA-256 is cb704a0f86b74df25f8586cffaa8f9869b4a8f8c95a0ee1b8321bda7adb617d6 across 1,944 lines.
The diff preserved disk_count and matches_disk=true at every affected record, isolating the defect to stale anchors rather than wrapper/module census drift.
existing_safeguards: generate_smoke_wrapper_map implements a non-mutating --check mode.
The generated records separately preserve disk counts and matches_disk booleans.
safeguard_gap: The check detects but does not repair drift, and the artifact remained committed after its inputs moved.
tests_present: tests/python/tooling tests exercise smoke-wrapper-map generation and drift semantics.
tests_missing: Same-change enforcement that regenerates the map whenever referenced documentation line positions change.
recommended_remediation: Run the canonical smoke-wrapper-map generator, review the line-only JSON diff, then rerun its --check mode and active-document/reference checks.
remediation_risk: Low; only generated documentation anchors change, but preserve exact counts and wrapper identities.
validation_rung: Generated-artifact check rung: generate_smoke_wrapper_map --check plus focused tooling tests and active-document reference validation. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Narrow recurrence of prior generated-context staleness family FR-057; that earlier finding was fixed, while these current line-anchor changes are new.

title: WebView lint budget is exceeded and its no-undef ratchet is stale
observed_behavior: npm run webview:lint:budget:check exits 1: total warnings are 1,389>1,387, complexity 136>133, max-lines-per-function 122>121, five file/pair categories increased, and two refreshCoordinator no-undef pairs decreased and require an intentional ratchet. queue/priority.js and runMonitorView.js have newly nonzero categories and therefore no current baseline record.
expected_invariant: WebView warning counts must not exceed the reviewed ratchet, and decreases must be intentionally accepted so the committed exact-pair baseline remains reproducible.
root_cause: WebView sources changed without either resolving the new warnings or intentionally updating the generated budget after review; simultaneous no-undef decreases left exact pair counts stale in the opposite direction.
failure_scenario: The canonical prework chain stops at lint-budget validation, hiding all later generated checks and blocking release validation; blindly rewriting the budget would normalize new complexity, unused-variable, and oversized-function debt.
evidence: webview:check parsed every enumerated asset successfully before lint-budget validation failed.

Exact failures: lifecycle/topbar.js complexity 2>0; progress/timelineView.js no-unused-vars 2>0; queue/priority.js max-lines-per-function 1>0; runMonitorView.js complexity 1>0; refreshCoordinator refreshQueuedOptions 5>4; lastQueue 2<3; renderHomeNextQueue 0<2.
Structured JSON inspection confirmed current aggregate 1,387, complexity 133, max-lines-per-function 121, 182 file records, and no baseline rows for queue/priority.js or runMonitorView.js.
Current budget SHA-256 is ad6098ceeffcf64b8dcd1dca43d896d58c31b165ad498ada3bf49ebd982a496a.
existing_safeguards: The check fails on aggregate, rule, file, and no-undef-pair increases.
A dedicated no-undef ratchet command accepts decreases separately from general budget writes.
safeguard_gap: The current source/budget pair is red, and the && prework chain prevents later checks from running unless invoked independently.
tests_missing: A structured aggregate result that continues all read-only prework checks after one failure while preserving each nonzero outcome.
recommended_remediation: Review and fix or explicitly accept each increased warning, run the dedicated no-undef ratchet for proven decreases, then rerun the full prework chain. Do not bulk-write the budget without reviewing source changes.
remediation_risk: Medium: accepting the budget without source review can permanently raise complexity and size debt; fixing warnings touches broad frontend code.
validation_rung: WebView parse/lint checks, exact budget check and ratchet, affected static tests, then full prework. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-worktree lint-ratchet failure; no structured current finding duplicated these exact aggregate and pair changes.

expected_invariant: A tracked generated navigation/advisory artifact must describe the current repository inputs and reproduce from its canonical generator before maintainers rely on its census.
root_cause: Twenty documents entered the scanner input set after the tracked report was generated, and this generator has no non-mutating --check mode to surface drift automatically.
failure_scenario: A documentation-maintenance pass treats the report as complete and overlooks 20 current archive candidates, understating housekeeping scope and the active-reference reconciliation needed before any move.
evidence: Current normalized report content SHA-256 is 60711f349f908019a14ab5fce873920bd1c057cc839e5df4366b6e6b901c2227; fresh normalized render SHA-256 is 18f6c5303f7208569c791d712eaf4456bc763ae16286b1aced6e5b17a0ce746f.
Fresh scan used as_of=2026-07-20 to preserve the report destination convention and returned 236 rows: 129 archive-candidate, 106 keep-active, and 1 review.
The in-memory comparison made no tracked write; it found 394 rendered lines versus 354 current split lines and 303 differing zip-aligned positions.
existing_safeguards: The scanner is explicitly advisory and dry-run only.
It classifies required active, generated, and architecture documents conservatively and records inbound references.
Focused tests cover archive-candidate scan behavior.
safeguard_gap: The generator can write an output but exposes no --check mode, so a stale checked-in census is not detected by the normal generated-artifact gates.

recommended_remediation: Regenerate the advisory scan with the canonical tool and the intended as-of date, review the 20 added candidates and their references, then add a non-mutating check mode to the generated validation suite.

title: Dependency atlas omits hundreds of current import relationships
observed_behavior: A clean temporary reproduction of the W12-owned dependency-atlas slice classifies 110 of 172 outputs as substantively stale: 53 PNG/SVG diagram pairs plus three CSVs and the root HTML. Another 31 PNGs are exact and 31 SVGs differ only by newline serialization.
expected_invariant: The dependency atlas must be reproducible from current Python AST imports so its module/domain diagrams, CSV edges, and linked HTML remain trustworthy navigation evidence.
root_cause: Python modules and imports changed after the atlas snapshot was generated, while the atlas generator has no --check mode and therefore did not fail the maintained generated-context gate.
failure_scenario: A reviewer follows stale domain diagrams or CSVs and misses current ownership/import relationships. The tracked module-edge CSV has 1,407 rows while current collection has 2,137, an omission of 730 relationships.
evidence: Two independent temporary Graphviz reproductions yielded the same category counts for all 172 W12-owned outputs: exact=31, newline-equivalent=31, PNG with changed SVG=53, and changed text=57.

Current AST collection found 769 modules, 2,137 module edges, 103 domains, 340 domain edges, and zero parse errors; tracked CSVs contain 1,407 module edges, 90 domain summary rows, and 309 domain edges.

Graphviz 15.0.0 rendered 98 detail diagrams, and the generated HTML resolved all 300 local links inside a disposable directory. The lossless manifest SHA-256 for the second run is 4f095017d6a736c92ed6ba9087151722d9d73f05874dfbaa632f2d73d5824a45.
Newline-equivalent SVGs were deliberately excluded from the finding, and no tracked atlas output was rewritten during reproduction.
existing_safeguards: The generator parses imports with ast and records parse errors.
It validates all generated HTML local links.
Focused tooling tests exercise atlas collection, rendering helpers, and output cleanup.
safeguard_gap: The generator has no --check mode, so its deterministic text/graph inputs can drift by hundreds of edges without a failing freshness gate.
tests_missing: A non-mutating full-output or semantic-manifest check that distinguishes content drift from platform newline serialization.
recommended_remediation: After source writers quiesce, regenerate the complete atlas with the pinned local Graphviz runtime, review the module/domain count changes, and add a semantic --check mode that normalizes text newlines while validating CSV, SVG, HTML, and paired PNG provenance.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: outputs are generated navigation only, but a blind rewrite could obscure an unintended architectural dependency increase unless the 730 added edges and 13 added domains are reviewed.
validation_rung: Full temporary atlas reproduction, exact/normalized manifest comparison, focused dependency-atlas tests, and HTML link validation. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Current broader atlas drift; AUDIT-FIND-W05-011 covers four other worker-owned atlas paths, while this finding strictly owns the 110 W12 paths listed here.

title: Frozen coverage captured eleven summaries beside transiently newer source identities
observed_behavior: In the frozen 6,064-row coverage snapshot, these eleven summary frontmatter hashes disagree with their corresponding source-row content hashes. Current worktree sources again match the summaries and the current full summary check does not name these eleven paths, so the mismatch was transient and is resolved at HEAD.
expected_invariant: A repository-audit baseline must freeze generated summaries and their authoritative source identities atomically so provenance can be verified within one snapshot.
root_cause: The central coverage universe was built while concurrent writers temporarily changed source documents/tests without changing these summary bytes; subsequent worktree settlement restored or replaced those source versions.
failure_scenario: A review merged against the frozen matrix could either claim these summaries are reproducible when their paired frozen source hash disagrees or incorrectly report a current defect that no longer exists at HEAD.
evidence: Snapshot-byte verification recovered 1,824 W12 summaries: 1,789 directly from matching worktree bytes and 35 from their frozen Git blobs. Exactly eleven declared source hashes disagreed with the paired frozen coverage source hash.
A current rerun of refresh_summaries --check reports exactly four different stale sources and does not name any of these eleven summary paths.
Current build_rows reports unchanged summary hashes for all eleven paths, while current source bytes again match their declared summary hashes.
existing_safeguards: Summary frontmatter records exact source SHA-256 values.
The ledger stores both artifact and source content identities.
The full summary check detects current source/summary drift.
safeguard_gap: The frozen coverage build did not take source and generated artifacts under a writer freeze, allowing a cross-file provenance pair to straddle transient states.
tests_missing: An atomic writer-freeze or generation-epoch assertion spanning coverage rows, source bytes, summaries, and PROJECT_INDEX.
recommended_remediation: Do not merge these frozen provenance claims as current truth. Rebuild the central matrix after writer freeze and rerun full summary checks; retain this resolved finding as evidence of why the current-HEAD addendum and rebaseline are required.
remediation_risk: Low; audit metadata only. Rebuilding before writers settle would simply reproduce the race.
validation_rung: Writer-freeze rebaseline plus full summary check and exact summary/source hash pairing. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Resolved path-local instance of the current AUDIT-FIND-COV-001 non-atomic generated-context family.

title: Seven release-packet summaries are stale outside the full summary check census
observed_behavior: Each listed summary declares a SHA-256 for its current unreleased change-packet JSON that differs from the packet current at HEAD. The full refresh_summaries --check command reports four tooling/test summaries but does not report these seven release-packet summaries.
expected_invariant: Every tracked generated summary must fingerprint its current declared source, and the canonical full freshness check must cover every tracked summary it presents as navigation evidence.
root_cause: The seven change packets changed after their summaries were generated, while the full summary check inventory excludes or otherwise fails to compare this release-packet summary class.
failure_scenario: After the four visible tooling summaries are refreshed, the canonical check can stop reporting summary drift even though seven release-evidence summaries still describe older packet status, validation, or touched-path metadata.
evidence: Exact current-HEAD frontmatter/source pairing found seven release-packet mismatches in addition to the four sources named by refresh_summaries --check.
All seven packet sources and summary paths are tracked/current build_rows inputs; each path has a current content identity in the 69-row addendum.
The current full check exited 1 with a six-line report naming only the four W12-002 tooling/test sources.
existing_safeguards: Summary frontmatter records the declared source path and SHA-256.
The full summary checker detects covered stale sources.
Change-packet validation independently checks packet schema and touched paths.
safeguard_gap: The canonical all-summary check does not surface this tracked release-packet summary class, so exact source/hash pairing is required to discover the drift.
tests_missing: A full-check coverage assertion that every tracked docs/generated/summaries path is either compared with its declared source or explicitly excluded with rationale.
recommended_remediation: Refresh these seven summaries after their packets settle, then extend the full summary check to enumerate tracked release-packet summaries and add a regression test for this class.
remediation_risk: Low for summary regeneration; wait for packet writers to settle to avoid immediate re-drift.
validation_rung: Exact current source/summary pairing, full summary check, focused summary-integrity tests, and change-packet validation. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-HEAD coverage gap discovered while reconciling the 69-row delta; W12-002 covers the four summaries the canonical check does report.
